findings: Closed stepped dou cuts read as timber rather than puffy cushions. Smaller branches reduce visible round-stick clutter.
Moss still reads as a continuous bright polygon sheet; neck still creates a second bulb-like silhouette. Stone cap fascia is too plain and block-like.
Bare high earthen bank beneath the hall is a large unsupported-looking smooth shape; shrub roots use analytic heights that diverge from the rendered triangular terrain.
Overall architecture-specific roof forms, material response, canopy shape, local garden structure and sunlight remain visually unaccepted.
